questions.solution: Each side is the diameter times the sine of its opposite angle. $BC = 12\sin 60^\circ = 6\sqrt{3}$ and $CA = 12\sin 45^\circ = 6\sqrt{2}$. The product is $36\sqrt{6}$.

questions.stem: A triangle has sides $13$, $14$ and $15$. Let $C$ be the angle opposite the side of length $15$. What is $\cos C$?
An isosceles triangle has two sides of length $4$, and the angle between them is $120^\circ$. Use $\cos 120^\circ = -\frac{1}{2}$. How long is the third side?
A parallelogram has sides $7$ and $8$ and one angle of $60^\circ$. How long is its longer diagonal?
questions.solution: The longer diagonal is opposite the $120^\circ$ angle. Use $\cos 120^\circ = -\frac{1}{2}$: $d^2 = 49 + 64 - 2(7)(8)\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = 113 + 56 = 169$, so $d = 13$.

questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, $a = 7$, $b = 5$ and $c = 8$, where each letter is the side opposite the angle of the same name. What is $\cos B$?

questions.skill: Drawing a helpful line (altitude, radius, diagonal)
questions.stem: The parallel sides of an isosceles trapezoid are 10 and 16 long, and each of its two equal slanted sides is 5 long. How far apart are the two parallel sides?
questions.solution: Draw a perpendicular from each end of the short side down to the long side. The long side is $16 - 10 = 6$ longer, so each end sticks out by $3$. Each slanted side is then the hypotenuse of a right triangle with a leg of 3 and hypotenuse 5, so the other leg is $\sqrt{25 - 9} = 4$. The distance between the parallel sides is 4.

questions.stem: A rectangle is 8 long and 15 wide. How long is its diagonal?
questions.solution: The diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 8 and 15: $8^2 + 15^2 = 64 + 225 = 289 = 17^2$. So the diagonal is 17. (23 is the sum of the sides.)

questions.stem: Triangles $ABC$ and $DBC$ share the side $BC$ as a base. The height of $ABC$ over $BC$ is 6 and the height of $DBC$ over $BC$ is 9. The area of $ABC$ is 20. What is the area of $DBC$?
questions.solution: With the same base, the area is proportional to the height. So the area of $DBC$ is $20 \cdot \frac{9}{6} = 30$. (Or: the base is $\frac{2 \cdot 20}{6} = \frac{20}{3}$, and $\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{20}{3} \cdot 9 = 30$.)

solve.work: Same base, area proportional to height: 20 * 9/6 = 30.

questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, point $D$ is on side $AB$ and point $E$ is on side $AC$, with $DE$ parallel to $BC$. $AD = 2$, $DB = 4$ and $DE = 5$. What is the length of $BC$?
questions.solution: Triangle $ADE$ is similar to triangle $ABC$. $AB = 2 + 4 = 6$, so the ratio of corresponding sides is $\frac{AB}{AD} = \frac{6}{2} = 3$. So $BC = 3 \cdot 5 = 15$. (10 only doubles $DE$, and 20 multiplies it by $DB$.)

solve.work: AB = 6, ADE ~ ABC with ratio 2:6 = 1:3, BC = 15.

questions.stem: A 2 meter stick standing straight up casts a shadow 3 meters long. At the same moment, a tree casts a shadow 15 meters long. How tall is the tree, in meters?
questions.solution: The sun's rays make the same angle for both, so the two right triangles are similar: $\frac{\text{height}}{15} = \frac{2}{3}$. The tree is $15 \cdot \frac{2}{3} = 10$ meters tall.

questions.stem: A 10 foot ladder leans against a straight wall. Its foot is 6 feet from the bottom of the wall on level ground. How many feet up the wall does the ladder reach?
questions.solution: The ladder, the wall and the ground form a right triangle with hypotenuse 10 and one leg 6. The height is $\sqrt{10^2 - 6^2} = \sqrt{64} = 8$ feet. (This is a 3-4-5 triangle doubled: 6, 8, 10.)

questions.skill: Angle chasing and reasoning about a figure
questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, $\angle A = 50^\circ$ and $\angle B = 60^\circ$. The side $BC$ is extended past $C$ to a point $D$. What is the measure of $\angle ACD$, in degrees?
questions.solution: An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two far interior angles: $50 + 60 = 110$. (Or: $\angle ACB = 180 - 50 - 60 = 70$, and $\angle ACD = 180 - 70 = 110$.)

questions.skill: Drawing a helpful line (altitude, radius, diagonal)
questions.stem: A triangle has sides of length 5, 5 and 6. What is its area?
questions.solution: Draw the altitude to the side of length 6. In an isosceles triangle it hits the middle of that side, so it splits the triangle into two right triangles with hypotenuse 5 and one leg 3. The altitude is $\sqrt{25 - 9} = 4$. The area is $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 6 \cdot 4 = 12$.

solve.work: Isosceles: altitude to 6 is sqrt(25 - 9) = 4, area = 6*4/2 = 12.

questions.stem: A triangle has area 24, and one of its sides is 8 long. How long is the altitude drawn to that side?
questions.solution: Area $= \frac{1}{2} \cdot \text{base} \cdot \text{height}$, so $24 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 8 \cdot h = 4h$ and $h = 6$. (3 forgets the factor of $\frac{1}{2}$, and 192 multiplies instead of dividing.)

questions.skill: Angle chasing and reasoning about a figure
questions.stem: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. Two of the angles on the same side of the transversal and between the parallel lines measure $(2x + 10)^\circ$ and $(3x + 20)^\circ$. What is $x$?
questions.solution: Angles between parallel lines and on the same side of the transversal add up to $180^\circ$. So $(2x + 10) + (3x + 20) = 180$, which gives $5x + 30 = 180$ and $x = 30$. (The angles are $70^\circ$ and $110^\circ$.)

solve.work: Same-side interior angles are supplementary: 5x + 30 = 180, x = 30.

questions.skill: Drawing a helpful line (altitude, radius, diagonal)
questions.stem: A triangle has two sides of length 13 and a third side of length 10. What is its area?
questions.solution: Draw the altitude to the side of length 10. It cuts that side into two parts of 5, so by the Pythagorean theorem its length is $\sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = 12$. The area is $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot 12 = 60$.

solve.work: Isosceles 13, 13, 10: altitude to base = sqrt(169 - 25) = 12, area = 10*12/2 = 60.

questions.skill: Drawing a helpful line (altitude, radius, diagonal)
questions.stem: A trapezoid has parallel sides of length 7 and 12. One of the other two sides is perpendicular to both of them. The fourth side is 13 long. How long is the perpendicular side?
questions.solution: Draw a line from the end of the short parallel side, parallel to the perpendicular side. It makes a right triangle with hypotenuse 13 and one leg $12 - 7 = 5$. The other leg is $\sqrt{13^2 - 5^2} = 12$, and it equals the perpendicular side. (8 is $13 - 5$ and 18 is $13 + 5$.)

solve.work: Right trapezoid: horizontal offset 12 - 7 = 5, slant 13, so height sqrt(169 - 25) = 12.

questions.skill: Drawing a helpful line (altitude, radius, diagonal)
questions.stem: A chord of length 8 is drawn in a circle of radius 5. How far is the chord from the center of the circle?
questions.solution: Draw the radius to one end of the chord, and the perpendicular from the center to the chord. It meets the chord at its midpoint, so a right triangle has hypotenuse 5 and one leg 4. The other leg is $\sqrt{25 - 16} = 3$.

questions.skill: Drawing a helpful line (altitude, radius, diagonal)
questions.stem: A rhombus has sides of length 5 and a shorter diagonal of length 6. How long is its longer diagonal?
questions.solution: The diagonals of a rhombus cross at right angles and cut each other in half. One half-diagonal is 3, so the other half is $\sqrt{5^2 - 3^2} = 4$, and the longer diagonal is 8. (4 is only half of it.)

solve.work: Diagonals bisect at right angles: halves 3 and 4 with side 5, longer diagonal 8.

questions.stem: A rectangular field is 20 meters wide and 21 meters long. How many meters is it from one corner to the opposite corner, in a straight line?
questions.solution: The diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 20 and 21: $20^2 + 21^2 = 400 + 441 = 841 = 29^2$.

questions.stem: Two hikers leave the same spot at the same time. One walks 9 km due north and the other walks 12 km due east. How far apart are they, in kilometers?
questions.solution: North and east make a right angle, so the distance is the hypotenuse: $\sqrt{9^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{225} = 15$. (21 adds the legs, 3 subtracts them and 225 forgets the square root.)

questions.stem: A right triangle has a hypotenuse of length 25 and one leg of length 7. How long is the other leg?
questions.solution: $\text{leg}^2 = 25^2 - 7^2 = 625 - 49 = 576$, so the other leg is 24.

questions.stem: Which set of three lengths can be the sides of a right triangle?
questions.solution:
A right triangle needs $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$ with $c$ the longest. $9^2 + 12^2 = 225 = 15^2$ works. The others give $145 
e 169$, $100 
e 121$ and $125 
e 144$.

questions.stem: A triangle has sides of length 6 and 9. The altitude drawn to the side of length 9 is 4. How long is the altitude drawn to the side of length 6?
questions.solution: The area is $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 9 \cdot 4 = 18$. Using the other side, $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 6 \cdot h = 18$, so $h = 6$.

solve.work: Area = 9*4/2 = 18; altitude to side 6 = 36/6 = 6 (sin of included angle 2/3, consistent).

questions.stem: A parallelogram has sides of length 6 and 10. The height drawn to the side of length 10 is 3. What is the height drawn to the side of length 6?
questions.solution: The area is base times height: $10 \cdot 3 = 30$. For the other side, $6 \cdot h = 30$, so $h = 5$. (1.8 divides the wrong way, 13 adds and 18 is $6 \cdot 3$.)

questions.stem: $ABCD$ is a square with side 10, and $M$ is the midpoint of side $CD$. What is the area of triangle $ABM$?
questions.solution: Triangle $ABM$ has base $AB = 10$, and its height is the distance between the lines $AB$ and $CD$, which is also 10. The area is $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot 10 = 50$, half the square.

solve.work: Base AB = 10, height from M to AB = 10, area 50.

questions.stem: The point $D$ is on side $BC$ of triangle $ABC$, with $BD = 4$ and $DC = 8$. The area of triangle $ABC$ is 36. What is the area of triangle $ADC$?
questions.solution: Triangles $ABD$ and $ADC$ have the same height from $A$, so their areas are in the ratio of their bases $4 : 8$. Triangle $ADC$ is $\frac{8}{12}$ of 36, which is 24.

solve.work: Same height from A; area ADC = (8/12)*36 = 24.

questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, the point $D$ is on $AB$ and $E$ is on $AC$, with $DE$ parallel to $BC$. $AD = 3$, $AB = 9$ and $DE = 4$. What is $BC$?
questions.solution: Triangles $ADE$ and $ABC$ are similar, with ratio $AD : AB = 3 : 9 = 1 : 3$. So $BC = 3 \cdot DE = 12$.

questions.stem: Two triangles are similar. A side of 6 in the smaller triangle matches a side of 9 in the larger. The perimeter of the smaller triangle is 20. What is the perimeter of the larger triangle?
questions.solution: The scale factor is $\frac{9}{6} = \frac{3}{2}$, and perimeters scale the same way: $20 \cdot \frac{3}{2} = 30$. (23 adds $3$, 26 adds 6, and $\frac{40}{3}$ scales the wrong way.)

questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, $M$ is the midpoint of $AB$ and $N$ is the midpoint of $AC$. $MN = 7$. How long is $BC$?
questions.solution: The segment joining two midpoints is parallel to the third side and half as long, so $BC = 2 \cdot 7 = 14$.

questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, $D$ is on $AB$ and $E$ is on $AC$, with $DE$ parallel to $BC$. $AD = 4$, $DB = 2$ and $AE = 6$. What is $EC$?
questions.solution: A line parallel to a side cuts the other two sides in the same ratio: $\frac{AD}{DB} = \frac{AE}{EC}$, so $\frac{4}{2} = \frac{6}{EC}$ and $EC = 3$.

questions.skill: Angle chasing and reasoning about a figure
questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, $\angle A = 40^\circ$ and $\angle B = 80^\circ$. The point $D$ is on side $AB$ and $CD$ bisects $\angle C$. What is $\angle ACD$, in degrees?
questions.solution: $\angle C = 180 - 40 - 80 = 60$. The bisector splits it in half, so $\angle ACD = 30$.

questions.skill: Angle chasing and reasoning about a figure
questions.stem: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is $30^\circ$. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.solution: The exterior angles of any convex polygon add up to $360^\circ$, so there are $\frac{360}{30} = 12$ of them, hence 12 sides.

questions.skill: Angle chasing and reasoning about a figure
questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, $AB = AC$ and $\angle B = 70^\circ$. What is $\angle A$, in degrees?
questions.solution: Equal sides $AB = AC$ mean equal base angles: $\angle C = \angle B = 70^\circ$. So $\angle A = 180 - 70 - 70 = 40$.

questions.skill: Angle chasing and reasoning about a figure
questions.stem: In triangle $PQR$, the exterior angle at $R$ (formed by extending $QR$ past $R$) is $125^\circ$ and $\angle P = 60^\circ$. What is $\angle Q$, in degrees?
questions.solution: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: $125 = 60 + \angle Q$, so $\angle Q = 65$. (55 is $180 - 125$.)

solve.work: Exterior angle at R = P + Q: 125 = 60 + Q, Q = 65.

questions.skill: Combining several ideas in one problem
questions.stem: A circle has radius 10 and center $O$. The chord $AB$ has length 12. What is the area of triangle $OAB$?
questions.solution: Draw the perpendicular from $O$ to $AB$. It meets $AB$ at its midpoint, 6 from $A$, so its length is $\sqrt{10^2 - 6^2} = 8$. The area is $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 12 \cdot 8 = 48$.

solve.work: Distance from O to AB = sqrt(100 - 36) = 8; area = 12*8/2 = 48.

questions.skill: Combining several ideas in one problem
questions.stem: Rectangle $ABCD$ has $AB = 12$ and its diagonal $AC = 13$. What is the area of the rectangle?
questions.solution: In right triangle $ABC$, $BC = \sqrt{13^2 - 12^2} = 5$. The area is $12 \cdot 5 = 60$. (156 is $12 \cdot 13$, and 30 is the area of one triangle.)

questions.skill: Combining several ideas in one problem
questions.stem: A rhombus has diagonals of length 6 and 8. What is the distance between two opposite sides of the rhombus?
questions.solution: The area is $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 6 \cdot 8 = 24$. The half-diagonals 3 and 4 give a side of $\sqrt{9 + 16} = 5$. Area equals side times distance, so the distance is $\frac{24}{5} = 4.8$.

solve.work: Area = 6*8/2 = 24; side = sqrt(9 + 16) = 5; distance between opposite sides = 24/5 = 4.8.

questions.skill: Drawing a helpful line (altitude, radius, diagonal)
questions.stem: In trapezoid $ABCD$, side $AB$ is parallel to side $CD$. $AB = 20$, $CD = 6$, $AD = 13$ and $BC = 15$. What is the area of the trapezoid?
questions.solution: Drop perpendiculars of the same height $h$ from $C$ and $D$ to $AB$. The two right triangles at the ends have bases that add up to $20 - 6 = 14$. A right triangle with hypotenuse 13 and base 5 has height 12, and one with hypotenuse 15 and base 9 has height 12, and $5 + 9 = 14$, so $h = 12$. (This is the only split that fits.) The area is $\frac{20 + 6}{2} \cdot 12 = 156$.

solve.work: Drop heights from D and C; projections a + b = 14, 169 - a^2 = 225 - b^2 so b^2 - a^2 = 56, b - a = 4, b = 9, a = 5, h = 12. Area = (20+6)/2*12 = 156. Legs leaning the same way would need b - a = 14 and b + a = 4, impossible.

questions.stem: A right triangle has legs 5 and 12 and hypotenuse 13. How long is the altitude drawn from the right angle to the hypotenuse?
questions.solution: Find the area two ways. Using the legs: $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 5 \cdot 12 = 30$. Using the hypotenuse as the base: $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 13 \cdot h = 30$. So $h = \frac{60}{13}$. (The other options forget a factor of 2, halve a leg, or divide by the sum of the legs.)

questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, point $D$ is on $AB$ and point $E$ is on $AC$, with $DE$ parallel to $BC$. $AD = 6$ and $DB = 3$, and the area of triangle $ADE$ is 36. What is the area of triangle $ABC$?
questions.solution: $AB = 6 + 3 = 9$, so triangle $ABC$ is similar to triangle $ADE$ with ratio $\frac{9}{6} = \frac{3}{2}$. Areas change by the square of the ratio, $\frac{9}{4}$. So the area of $ABC$ is $36 \cdot \frac{9}{4} = 81$.

questions.stem: A rectangle has perimeter 34 and diagonal 13. What is its area?
questions.solution: Let the sides be $a$ and $b$. Then $a + b = 17$ and $a^2 + b^2 = 13^2 = 169$. Since $(a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2$, we get $289 = 169 + 2ab$, so $ab = 60$. (The sides are 5 and 12.)

questions.skill: Drawing a helpful line (altitude, radius, diagonal)
questions.stem: A rhombus has diagonals of length 16 and 12. How long is each of its sides?
questions.solution: The diagonals of a rhombus cross at right angles and cut each other in half. Each side is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs $8$ and $6$, so it is $\sqrt{64 + 36} = 10$.

questions.skill: Angle chasing and reasoning about a figure
questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, $AB = AC$ and $\angle A = 36^\circ$. The point $D$ is on side $AC$ and $BD$ bisects $\angle B$. What is the measure of $\angle BDC$, in degrees?
questions.solution: The base angles are $\frac{180 - 36}{2} = 72^\circ$ each, so $\angle ABC = 72^\circ$ and the bisector makes $\angle ABD = 36^\circ$. In triangle $ABD$, the exterior angle at $D$ is $\angle BDC = \angle A + \angle ABD = 36 + 36 = 72$ degrees.

solve.work: Base angles 72; angle DBC = 36; in BDC: angle BDC = 180 - 36 - 72 = 72.

questions.stem: A triangle has sides of length 10, 14 and 18. A second triangle is formed by joining the midpoints of the three sides. What is the perimeter of the second triangle?
questions.solution: A segment joining two midpoints is parallel to the third side and half as long. So each side of the new triangle is half of a side of the old one, and the perimeter is half of $10 + 14 + 18 = 42$, which is 21.

solve.work: Midsegment triangle has half the perimeter: 42/2 = 21.

questions.stem: Triangle $ABC$ has area 60. The point $D$ is on side $BC$ with $BD : DC = 2 : 3$. What is the area of triangle $ABD$?
questions.solution: Triangles $ABD$ and $ADC$ have the same height from $A$ to line $BC$, so their areas are in the ratio of their bases, $2 : 3$. Triangle $ABD$ has $\frac{2}{5}$ of the area: $60 \cdot \frac{2}{5} = 24$.

solve.work: Same height from A: area ABD = 60 * 2/5 = 24.

questions.stem: A circle has radius 13. A chord is 5 units from the center of the circle. How long is the chord?
questions.solution: The perpendicular from the center to a chord bisects it. Draw a radius to one end of the chord: it is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 5 and half the chord. Half the chord is $\sqrt{169 - 25} = 12$, so the chord is 24. (12 is only half the chord.)

questions.stem: $ABCD$ is a square with side 6. $E$ is the midpoint of side $BC$ and $F$ is the midpoint of side $CD$. What is the area of triangle $AEF$?
questions.solution: Subtract the three corner triangles from the square. Triangle $ABE$ has legs 6 and 3: area 9. Triangle $ADF$ also has area 9. Triangle $ECF$ has legs 3 and 3: area $4.5$. So the area of $AEF$ is $36 - 9 - 9 - 4.5 = 13.5$.

questions.skill: Drawing a helpful line (altitude, radius, diagonal)
questions.stem: The parallel sides of an isosceles trapezoid are 8 and 20, and each of the two equal slanted sides is 10. What is the area of the trapezoid?
questions.solution: Draw the two altitudes from the ends of the short side. Each cuts off $\frac{20 - 8}{2} = 6$ from the long side, so the height is $\sqrt{10^2 - 6^2} = 8$. The area is $\frac{8 + 20}{2} \cdot 8 = 112$.

questions.skill: Drawing a helpful line (altitude, radius, diagonal)
questions.stem: In a circle of radius 10, two parallel chords have lengths 12 and 16, and both lie on the same side of the center. How far apart are the two chords?
questions.solution: The chord of length 12 is $\sqrt{100 - 36} = 8$ from the center, and the chord of length 16 is $\sqrt{100 - 64} = 6$ from it. On the same side, they are $8 - 6 = 2$ apart. (14 is the distance if they were on opposite sides.)

solve.work: Distances: chord 12 -> sqrt(100 - 36) = 8; chord 16 -> sqrt(100 - 64) = 6. Same side: 8 - 6 = 2.

questions.skill: Drawing a helpful line (altitude, radius, diagonal)
questions.stem: Two circles, of radii 4 and 9, touch each other from the outside. A straight line touches both circles. What is the distance between the two points where the line touches them?
questions.solution: The centers are $4 + 9 = 13$ apart. Draw from the smaller center a line parallel to the tangent, to form a right triangle with hypotenuse 13 and a leg $9 - 4 = 5$. The other leg, equal to the distance between the touching points, is $\sqrt{169 - 25} = 12$.

solve.work: Centers 13 apart, radii differ by 5; external common tangent length sqrt(169 - 25) = 12 (= 2*sqrt(4*9)). The tangent at the touching point meets both circles at one point, so 'the two points' excludes it.

questions.skill: Drawing a helpful line (altitude, radius, diagonal)
questions.stem: $ABCD$ is a convex quadrilateral with a right angle at $B$. $AB = 3$, $BC = 4$, $CD = 12$ and $DA = 13$. What is its area?
questions.solution: Draw the diagonal $AC$. In the right triangle $ABC$, $AC = 5$. Then triangle $ACD$ has sides 5, 12, 13, so it is right-angled at $C$. The area is $\frac{3 \cdot 4}{2} + \frac{5 \cdot 12}{2} = 6 + 30 = 36$.

questions.stem: A rectangle has a diagonal of length 25 and one side of length 7. What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
questions.solution: The other side is $\sqrt{25^2 - 7^2} = 24$. The perimeter is $2(7 + 24) = 62$. (31 is half the perimeter, 168 is the area.)

questions.stem: What is the distance between the points $(1, 2)$ and $(9, 8)$ on a coordinate plane?
questions.solution: The horizontal change is $9 - 1 = 8$ and the vertical change is $8 - 2 = 6$. The distance is the hypotenuse $\sqrt{8^2 + 6^2} = 10$.

questions.stem: A 25 foot ladder leans against a vertical wall, with its foot 7 feet from the wall on level ground. The top of the ladder slides 4 feet down the wall. How many feet does the foot of the ladder move away from the wall?
questions.solution: At first the ladder reaches $\sqrt{25^2 - 7^2} = 24$ feet up. After sliding 4 feet it reaches 20 feet, so the foot is $\sqrt{625 - 400} = 15$ feet out. It moved $15 - 7 = 8$ feet.

solve.work: Top at sqrt(625 - 49) = 24, slides to 20; foot at sqrt(625 - 400) = 15; moves 15 - 7 = 8.

questions.stem: A right triangle has legs of length 10 and 24. How long is the line from the right-angle vertex to the midpoint of the hypotenuse?
questions.solution: The hypotenuse is $\sqrt{100 + 576} = 26$. The midpoint of the hypotenuse is the center of the circle through all three vertices, so it is as far from the right-angle vertex as from the ends: $\frac{26}{2} = 13$.

questions.stem: $ABCD$ is a rectangle with $AB = 12$ and $BC = 8$. The point $P$ is somewhere on side $CD$. What is the area of triangle $ABP$?
questions.solution: Triangle $ABP$ has base $AB = 12$. Its height is the distance from $P$ to line $AB$, which is 8 wherever $P$ is on $CD$. The area is $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 12 \cdot 8 = 48$.

solve.work: Base AB = 12, height BC = 8 wherever P is on CD: area 48.

questions.stem: The medians of triangle $ABC$ meet at the point $G$. The area of triangle $ABC$ is 54. What is the area of triangle $ABG$?
questions.solution: The three medians cut the triangle into six triangles of equal area, and $ABG$ is two of them: $\frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}$ of the whole. So the area is $\frac{54}{3} = 18$.

solve.work: Centroid splits triangle into three equal areas: 54/3 = 18.

questions.stem: In trapezoid $ABCD$, side $AB$ is parallel to $CD$, with $AB = 14$ and $CD = 6$. The distance between the parallel sides is 5. The diagonal $AC$ splits the trapezoid into two triangles. How much larger is the area of triangle $ABC$ than the area of triangle $ACD$?
questions.solution: Both triangles have height 5. Triangle $ABC$ has base 14, so its area is 35; triangle $ACD$ has base 6, so its area is 15. The difference is 20. (35 is the area of $ABC$ alone.)

questions.stem: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram with area 60, and $M$ is the midpoint of side $AB$. What is the area of triangle $MCD$?
questions.solution: Triangle $MCD$ has base $CD$, the same as the parallelogram's, and the same height. So its area is half the parallelogram's: 30.

solve.work: Triangle MCD has base CD and the parallelogram's full height: half the area, 30.

questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, the point $D$ is on $AB$ and $E$ is on $AC$, with $DE$ parallel to $BC$. $AD = 4$ and $DB = 6$, and the perimeter of triangle $ADE$ is 14. What is the perimeter of triangle $ABC$?
questions.solution: $AB = 10$, so the scale factor from $ADE$ to $ABC$ is $\frac{10}{4}$. The perimeter of $ABC$ is $14 \cdot \frac{10}{4} = 35$.

questions.stem: The diagonals of trapezoid $ABCD$ meet at $P$, with $AB$ parallel to $CD$, $AB = 4$ and $CD = 10$. What is the ratio of the area of triangle $ABP$ to the area of triangle $CDP$?
questions.solution: Triangles $ABP$ and $CDP$ are similar, with ratio of sides $4 : 10 = 2 : 5$. Areas go as the square of that ratio: $4 : 25$. (2 : 5 is the ratio of the sides, not the areas.)

questions.stem: A girl 1.5 meters tall stands 4 meters from the base of a lamp post. Her shadow is 2 meters long, so the tip of the shadow is 6 meters from the base of the post. How tall is the lamp post, in meters?
questions.solution: The girl and her shadow, and the post and the line from its base to the shadow tip, make similar right triangles. So $\frac{\text{post}}{6} = \frac{1.5}{2}$, which gives a height of $4.5$ meters.

solve.work: Similar triangles from shadow tip: H/6 = 1.5/2, H = 4.5.

questions.stem: Triangle $ABC$ has a right angle at $C$. The point $D$ is on $AB$ with $CD$ perpendicular to $AB$. $AC = 6$ and $AB = 10$. What is $AD$?
questions.solution: Triangles $ADC$ and $ACB$ are similar (they share angle $A$ and each has a right angle), so $\frac{AD}{AC} = \frac{AC}{AB}$ and $AD = \frac{36}{10} = 3.6$. (6.4 is $DB$ and 8 is $BC$.)

questions.skill: Angle chasing and reasoning about a figure
questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, $\angle A = 80^\circ$. The bisectors of angles $B$ and $C$ meet at the point $I$. What is $\angle BIC$, in degrees?
questions.solution: $\angle B + \angle C = 100^\circ$. Half of each is bisected, so $\angle IBC + \angle ICB = 50^\circ$. Then $\angle BIC = 180 - 50 = 130$.

questions.skill: Angle chasing and reasoning about a figure
questions.stem: Five angles of a convex hexagon are $110^\circ$ each. What is the sixth angle, in degrees?
questions.solution: The angles of a hexagon add up to $(6 - 2) \cdot 180 = 720$. Five angles use $550$, leaving $720 - 550 = 170$.

questions.skill: Angle chasing and reasoning about a figure
questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, $AB = AC$ and $\angle BAC = 100^\circ$. The point $D$ is on $BC$ with $BD = BA$. What is $\angle CAD$, in degrees?
questions.solution: $\angle B = \angle C = 40^\circ$. Triangle $BAD$ has $BA = BD$, so $\angle BAD = \frac{180 - 40}{2} = 70$. Then $\angle CAD = 100 - 70 = 30$.

solve.work: B = C = 40. Triangle ABD isosceles with BA = BD and apex 40: BAD = 70. CAD = 100 - 70 = 30.

questions.skill: Angle chasing and reasoning about a figure
questions.stem: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram with $\angle A = 70^\circ$. The bisectors of angles $A$ and $B$ meet at $P$. What is $\angle APB$, in degrees?
questions.solution: Angles $A$ and $B$ are supplementary, so $\angle A + \angle B = 180$. In triangle $APB$ the base angles add to $\frac{180}{2} = 90$, so $\angle APB = 90$.

solve.work: A + B = 180, so halves sum to 90; APB = 180 - 90 = 90.

questions.skill: Combining several ideas in one problem
questions.stem: A right triangle has legs 8 and 15. What is the radius of the circle that touches all three of its sides (the circle inside the triangle)?
questions.solution: The hypotenuse is 17, the area is $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 8 \cdot 15 = 60$ and the perimeter is 40. Joining the center to the three sides splits the area into three triangles of height $r$: $60 = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 40 \cdot r$, so $r = 3$.

questions.skill: Combining several ideas in one problem
questions.stem: A rectangle is 5 by 12. A circle passes through all four of its corners. What is the radius of the circle?
questions.solution: A diagonal of the rectangle is a diameter, because the right angle at a corner sits on the circle. The diagonal is $\sqrt{25 + 144} = 13$, so the radius is 6.5.

questions.skill: Combining several ideas in one problem
questions.stem: A quadrilateral has diagonals of lengths 10 and 14 that cross at a right angle. What is its area?
questions.solution: The diagonals cut the quadrilateral into four right triangles. Their total area is $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot 14 = 70$.

questions.stem: A triangle has sides of length 13, 14 and 15. How long is the altitude drawn to the side of length 15? Give your answer as a decimal.
questions.solution: First find the area. Draw the altitude $h$ to the side of length 14, cutting it into $x$ and $14 - x$: $13^2 - x^2 = 15^2 - (14 - x)^2$ gives $169 - x^2 = 225 - 196 + 28x - x^2$, so $x = 5$ and $h = 12$. The area is $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 14 \cdot 12 = 84$. Then the altitude to the side 15 satisfies $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 15 \cdot h = 84$, so $h = \frac{168}{15} = 11.2$.

solve.work: Heron: s = 21, area = sqrt(21*8*7*6) = 84. Altitude to 15 = 168/15 = 11.2.

questions.stem: In trapezoid $ABCD$, side $AB$ is parallel to side $CD$, with $AB = 6$ and $CD = 9$. The diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ cross at $P$, and $AC = 20$. What is the length of $AP$?
questions.solution: Triangles $APB$ and $CPD$ are similar (the parallel sides give equal alternate angles, and the angles at $P$ are vertical angles). So $\frac{AP}{PC} = \frac{AB}{CD} = \frac{6}{9} = \frac{2}{3}$. Then $AP = \frac{2}{5} \cdot 20 = 8$. (12 is $PC$.)

questions.skill: Angle chasing and reasoning about a figure
questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, $\angle B = 50^\circ$ and $\angle C = 70^\circ$. The point $D$ is on side $BC$ with $AD$ perpendicular to $BC$, and the point $E$ is on side $BC$ with $AE$ bisecting $\angle BAC$. What is the measure of $\angle DAE$, in degrees?
questions.solution: $\angle BAC = 180 - 50 - 70 = 60^\circ$, so $\angle BAE = 30^\circ$. In right triangle $ABD$, $\angle BAD = 90 - 50 = 40^\circ$. So $\angle DAE = 40 - 30 = 10$ degrees.

solve.work: Angle A = 60. Angle BAD = 90 - 50 = 40, angle BAE = 30, DAE = 10.

questions.skill: Drawing a helpful line (altitude, radius, diagonal)
questions.stem: $ABCD$ is a rectangle with $AB = 8$ and $BC = 6$. The point $E$ is on diagonal $BD$ and $AE$ is perpendicular to $BD$. How long is $AE$? Give your answer as a decimal.
questions.solution: Draw diagonal $BD$: $BD = \sqrt{64 + 36} = 10$. Triangle $ABD$ is a right triangle with legs 6 and 8, so its area is $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 8 \cdot 6 = 24$. With $BD$ as base, $AE$ is the height: $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot AE = 24$, so $AE = 4.8$.

questions.skill: Drawing a helpful line (altitude, radius, diagonal)
questions.stem: In a circle of radius 13, two parallel chords have lengths 10 and 24, and they lie on opposite sides of the center. How far apart are the two chords?
questions.solution: Draw a radius to one end of each chord. The half-chords are 5 and 12, so the distances from the center are $\sqrt{169 - 25} = 12$ for the chord of length 10 and $\sqrt{169 - 144} = 5$ for the chord of length 24. On opposite sides of the center, the distance between them is $12 + 5 = 17$. (7 is the distance if they were on the same side.)

solve.work: Distances from center: sqrt(169-25) = 12 and sqrt(169-144) = 5; opposite sides, 17 apart.

questions.skill: Angle chasing and reasoning about a figure
questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, $AB = AC$. The point $D$ is on side $AC$ so that $AD = BD = BC$. What is the measure of $\angle A$, in degrees?
questions.solution: Let $\angle A = x$. Since $AD = BD$, $\angle ABD = x$, so the exterior angle $\angle BDC = 2x$. Since $BC = BD$, $\angle BCD = 2x$ too. As $AB = AC$, $\angle ABC = \angle C = 2x$, so $\angle DBC = 2x - x = x$. In triangle $BDC$: $x + 2x + 2x = 180$, so $x = 36$.

solve.work: Let angle A = x. AD = BD so angle ABD = x; angle BDC = 2x; BD = BC so angle C = 2x = angle ABC. x + 4x = 180, x = 36.

questions.stem: Triangle $ABC$ has a right angle at $C$. The point $D$ is on $AB$ with $CD$ perpendicular to $AB$. $AD = 4$ and $DB = 9$. What is the length of $CD$?
questions.solution: Triangles $ACD$ and $CBD$ are similar (each has a right angle at $D$, and $\angle ACD = \angle B$). So $\frac{CD}{AD} = \frac{DB}{CD}$, which gives $CD^2 = 4 \cdot 9 = 36$ and $CD = 6$. (36 is $CD^2$, and $\frac{13}{2}$ is the average of 4 and 9.)

solve.work: Altitude to hypotenuse: CD^2 = AD*DB = 36, CD = 6.

questions.stem: A point $P$ is inside an equilateral triangle. Its distances to the three sides are 2, 3 and 4. What is the length of the altitude of the equilateral triangle?
questions.solution: Join $P$ to the three corners to cut the triangle into three triangles whose bases are the sides (each of length $s$) and whose heights are 2, 3 and 4. Their areas add up to $\frac{1}{2}s(2 + 3 + 4)$. The whole triangle has area $\frac{1}{2}s \cdot h$. So $h = 2 + 3 + 4 = 9$. (3 is the average distance, and 24 is the product.)

solve.work: Viviani: the sum of distances equals the altitude, 2 + 3 + 4 = 9.

questions.stem: A rectangular box is 2 long, 3 wide and 6 high. What is the distance between two opposite corners of the box (the longest straight segment inside it)?
questions.solution: The diagonal of the base is $\sqrt{2^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{13}$. The space diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs $\sqrt{13}$ and 6: $\sqrt{13 + 36} = \sqrt{49} = 7$. (In general, $d^2 = 2^2 + 3^2 + 6^2 = 49$.)

questions.stem: $ABCD$ is a rectangle and $P$ is a point inside it with $PA = 2$, $PB = 5$ and $PC = 11$. What is $PD$?
questions.solution: Draw a line through $P$ parallel to $AB$ and another parallel to $AD$. Using the right triangles this makes, one can show that $PA^2 + PC^2 = PB^2 + PD^2$ for any point inside a rectangle. So $4 + 121 = 25 + PD^2$, $PD^2 = 100$ and $PD = 10$.

solve.work: British flag theorem: PA^2 + PC^2 = PB^2 + PD^2: 4 + 121 = 25 + PD^2, PD = 10.

questions.skill: Drawing a helpful line (altitude, radius, diagonal)
questions.stem: $ABCD$ is a trapezoid with $AB$ parallel to $CD$, $AB = 25$ and $CD = 4$. The other sides are $AD = 10$ and $BC = 17$. What is the area of the trapezoid?
questions.solution: Drop perpendiculars from $C$ and $D$ to $AB$, at distance $h$. They cut off lengths $x$ (beside $AD$) and $y$ (beside $BC$) with $x + y = 25 - 4 = 21$. Then $x^2 + h^2 = 100$ and $y^2 + h^2 = 289$, so $y^2 - x^2 = 189$ and $y - x = 9$. Thus $y = 15$, $x = 6$ and $h = 8$. The area is $\frac{25 + 4}{2} \cdot 8 = 116$.

questions.skill: Drawing a helpful line (altitude, radius, diagonal)
questions.stem: A circle has radius 25. Two parallel chords of lengths 14 and 40 lie on the same side of the center. How far apart are they?
questions.solution: The chord of length 14 is $\sqrt{625 - 49} = 24$ from the center, and the chord of length 40 is $\sqrt{625 - 400} = 15$ from it. On the same side, they are $24 - 15 = 9$ apart. (39 is the distance if they were on opposite sides.)

questions.skill: Drawing a helpful line (altitude, radius, diagonal)
questions.stem: Triangle $ABC$ has $AB = 10$, $AC = 17$ and $BC = 21$. The point $D$ is the foot of the altitude from $A$ to $BC$. How long is $AD$?

questions.skill: Drawing a helpful line (altitude, radius, diagonal)
questions.stem: Two circles have radii 3 and 5, and their centers are 17 apart. A straight line touches both circles and crosses the segment joining their centers. What is the distance between the two points where the line touches the circles?
questions.solution: Extend the radius of the first circle to its touching point, past the line, by the length of the second circle's radius. The end point and the two centers form a right triangle with hypotenuse 17 and one leg $3 + 5 = 8$. The other leg is $\sqrt{289 - 64} = 15$, and it equals the distance between the touching points.

questions.stem: A rectangular box is 12 long and 4 wide. The longest straight segment that fits inside it, from one corner to the opposite corner, is 13. How high is the box?
questions.solution: The space diagonal satisfies $12^2 + 4^2 + h^2 = 13^2$. So $144 + 16 + h^2 = 169$, giving $h^2 = 9$ and $h = 3$.

questions.stem: The three sides of a right triangle are consecutive even whole numbers. What is its perimeter?
questions.solution: Let the sides be $x$, $x + 2$ and $x + 4$. Then $x^2 + (x + 2)^2 = (x + 4)^2$, which simplifies to $x^2 - 4x - 12 = 0$, so $x = 6$. The sides are 6, 8, 10 and the perimeter is 24.

questions.stem: A right triangle has hypotenuse 17, and its two legs differ in length by 7. What is the area of the triangle?
questions.solution: Let the legs be $a$ and $b$ with $a - b = 7$. Then $(a - b)^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab$, so $49 = 289 - 2ab$ and $ab = 120$. The area is $\frac{ab}{2} = 60$. (The legs are 8 and 15.)

questions.stem: Two chords $AB$ and $AC$ of a circle start at the same point $A$ and meet at a right angle. $AB = 6$ and $AC = 8$. What is the radius of the circle?
questions.solution: A right angle at $A$ on the circle means that $BC$ is a diameter. By the Pythagorean theorem, $BC = \sqrt{36 + 64} = 10$, so the radius is 5.

solve.work: Inscribed right angle at A: BC is a diameter = 10, radius 5.

questions.stem: Triangle $ABC$ has area 120. The point $D$ is the midpoint of $BC$, and $E$ is the point on $AD$ with $AE : ED = 1 : 2$. What is the area of triangle $ABE$?
questions.solution: Triangle $ABD$ has half the area of $ABC$, which is 60. Triangles $ABE$ and $ABD$ share the vertex $B$, and $AE$ is $\frac{1}{3}$ of $AD$, so $ABE$ has $\frac{1}{3}$ of 60: 20.

questions.stem: $ABCD$ is a rectangle and $P$ is a point inside it. The triangles $PAB$, $PBC$ and $PCD$ have areas 12, 20 and 30. What is the area of triangle $PDA$?
questions.solution: The triangles $PAB$ and $PCD$ together fill half the rectangle (their heights add to the rectangle's width), and so do $PBC$ and $PDA$. So $12 + 30 = 20 + PDA$, giving $PDA = 22$. (42 is half the rectangle.)

solve.work: PAB + PCD = PBC + PDA = half the rectangle: 42 = 20 + x, x = 22.

questions.stem: Triangle $ABC$ has $AB = AC = 10$ and $BC = 12$. The point $P$ is anywhere on side $BC$. What is the sum of the distances from $P$ to the lines $AB$ and $AC$?
questions.solution: The height from $A$ is $\sqrt{100 - 36} = 8$, so the area is $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 12 \cdot 8 = 48$. Triangles $ABP$ and $ACP$ together make area 48: $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot d_1 + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot d_2 = 48$, so $d_1 + d_2 = \frac{96}{10} = 9.6$.

solve.work: Height 8, area 48. Area = (10*d1 + 10*d2)/2, so d1 + d2 = 9.6.

questions.stem: In trapezoid $ABCD$, $AB$ is parallel to $CD$, with $AB = 20$ and $CD = 12$. The area of the trapezoid is 128. The diagonals meet at $P$. What is the area of triangle $APB$?
questions.solution: $\frac{20 + 12}{2} \cdot h = 128$ gives $h = 8$. Triangle $ABC$ has area $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 20 \cdot 8 = 80$. The diagonals cut each other in the ratio $AP : PC = 20 : 12 = 5 : 3$, so $APB$ is $\frac{5}{8}$ of $ABC$: $80 \cdot \frac{5}{8} = 50$.

solve.work: Height h: (32/2)h = 128, h = 8. P splits height 20:12, so APB height 5; area 20*5/2 = 50.

questions.stem: Triangle $ABC$ has a right angle at $C$. The point $D$ is on $AB$ with $CD$ perpendicular to $AB$, and $AD = 9$ and $DB = 16$. What is the area of triangle $ABC$?
questions.solution: Triangles $ADC$ and $CDB$ are similar, so $\frac{CD}{9} = \frac{16}{CD}$ and $CD^2 = 144$, $CD = 12$. The hypotenuse is $AB = 25$, so the area is $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 25 \cdot 12 = 150$.

questions.stem: In trapezoid $ABCD$, the parallel sides are $AB = 12$ and $CD = 20$, and the diagonals meet at $P$. A line through $P$ parallel to $AB$ meets the legs at $E$ and $F$. What is the length of $EF$?
questions.solution: Triangles $APB$ and $CPD$ are similar, so $AP : AC = 12 : 32$. In triangle $ADC$, the line through $P$ parallel to $DC$ gives $EP = 20 \cdot \frac{12}{32} = 7.5$. By symmetry $PF = 7.5$, so $EF = 15$. (16 is the average of 12 and 20.)

questions.stem: A right triangle has legs of 20 and 30. A square is placed so that one corner is the right-angle vertex, two sides run along the legs, and the opposite corner lies on the hypotenuse. What is the side of the square?
questions.solution: Let the side be $s$. The small triangle above the square is similar to the whole one: along the leg of 20, the part left over is $20 - s$, and $\frac{20 - s}{20} = \frac{s}{30}$. So $30(20 - s) = 20s$, giving $600 = 50s$ and $s = 12$.

questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, $AB = 6$, $AC = 9$ and $BC = 10$. The bisector of angle $A$ meets $BC$ at $D$. What is $BD$?
questions.solution: An angle bisector divides the opposite side in the ratio of the adjacent sides: $BD : DC = AB : AC = 6 : 9 = 2 : 3$. So $BD = \frac{2}{5} \cdot 10 = 4$.

questions.skill: Angle chasing and reasoning about a figure
questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$, $AB = AC$. The point $D$ is on $BC$ and the point $E$ is on $AC$, with $AD = AE$. $\angle BAD = 30^\circ$. What is $\angle EDC$, in degrees?
questions.solution: Let $\angle B = \angle C = x$ and $\angle EDC = z$. The exterior angle $\angle ADC = x + 30$. Since $AD = AE$, $\angle ADE = \angle AED = x + z$ (the last by the exterior angle at $E$ of triangle $EDC$). Then $\angle ADC = \angle ADE + z$ gives $x + 30 = x + 2z$, so $z = 15$.

questions.skill: Angle chasing and reasoning about a figure
questions.stem: The quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in a circle, and $\angle ABC$ is twice $\angle ADC$. What is $\angle ADC$, in degrees?
questions.solution: Opposite angles of an inscribed quadrilateral add to $180^\circ$. With $\angle ADC = x$ and $\angle ABC = 2x$, $3x = 180$ and $x = 60$. (120 is $\angle ABC$.)

questions.skill: Angle chasing and reasoning about a figure
questions.stem: What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 5:12, in degrees?
questions.solution: The minute hand is at $12 \cdot 6 = 72^\circ$ from the 12. The hour hand moves $30^\circ$ per hour and $0.5^\circ$ per minute, so it is at $5 \cdot 30 + 12 \cdot 0.5 = 156^\circ$. The difference is $156 - 72 = 84^\circ$.

questions.skill: Angle chasing and reasoning about a figure
questions.stem: Triangle $ABC$ has a right angle at $C$ and $\angle A = 24^\circ$. The line $CD$ is the altitude to the hypotenuse and $CM$ is the median to the hypotenuse, with $D$ and $M$ on $AB$. What is $\angle DCM$, in degrees?
questions.solution: $\angle B = 66^\circ$. The median to the hypotenuse equals half of it, so $MC = MB$ and $\angle MCB = 66$. In the right triangle $CDB$, $\angle DCB = 90 - 66 = 24$. So $\angle DCM = 66 - 24 = 42$.

questions.skill: Combining several ideas in one problem
questions.stem: A right triangle has legs 6 and 8. A circle has its center on the hypotenuse and touches both legs. What is its radius?
questions.solution: Join the center to the two touching points and to the right-angle vertex. The two legs form triangles of height $r$ over each leg, and together they fill the triangle: $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 6 \cdot r + \frac{1}{2} \cdot 8 \cdot r = 24$. So $7r = 24$ and $r = \frac{24}{7}$.

solve.work: Center (r, r) on hypotenuse x/8 + y/6 = 1 with legs on axes: r(1/8 + 1/6) = 1, r = 24/7.

questions.skill: Combining several ideas in one problem
questions.stem: An isosceles triangle has sides 17, 17 and 16. What is the radius of the circle that touches all three sides (the circle inside the triangle)?
questions.solution: The altitude to the side of 16 is $\sqrt{289 - 64} = 15$, so the area is $\frac{1}{2} \cdot 16 \cdot 15 = 120$. The perimeter is 50. The radius is area over half the perimeter: $\frac{120}{25} = 4.8$.

questions.skill: Combining several ideas in one problem
questions.stem: A rectangular sheet of paper $ABCD$ has $AB = 12$ and $BC = 16$. It is folded so that corner $C$ lands exactly on corner $A$. How long is the crease (the fold line)?
questions.solution: The crease is the perpendicular bisector of the diagonal $AC$, and $AC = 20$. Let the crease meet $AC$ at its midpoint $O$ and $BC$ at $E$. Triangles $COE$ and $CBA$ are similar (shared angle $C$, right angles at $O$ and $B$), so $OE = OC \cdot \frac{AB}{BC} = 10 \cdot \frac{12}{16} = 7.5$. The crease is symmetric about $O$, so its length is 15.

solve.work: Crease is the perpendicular bisector of AC (length 20) inside the rectangle; length = 20*12/16 = 15 (half crease = 10*tan, 10*(12/16) = 7.5).
